p1-text.text:
The Lighthouse Keeper's Ledger
Each evening the keeper climbed ninety-two steps to light the lamp, then wrote the weather in a narrow green ledger. Fog came in from the north on most nights in autumn, and the horn sounded every thirty seconds until dawn. A supply boat arrived on the first Tuesday of each month, bringing flour, lamp oil, and letters from the mainland. In 1931 the ledger records a storm that lasted four days; the keeper counted eleven ships passing safely and one fishing boat that did not.
